messages:
sam-support: FYI customer (ACME) opened an urgent ticket — their service in prod VPC intermittently gets NXDOMAIN for api.acme.internal after last-night migration. App errors: downstream 502s + name resolution failures. Can someone triage?

acme-customer: seeing this from our side too — pods started failing ~00:45 UTC, rolling restarts didn't help. No LB changes on our end.

dmitri-netops: Can you paste a quick `dig` from a failing pod and node resolver config? Also which VPC ID/account did the migration move them to?

acme-customer: pasted outputs below (redacted):
```
# inside pod (busybox)
$ dig @10.0.2.2 api.acme.internal +short
# <no output>

$ dig @10.0.2.2 api.acme.internal SOA +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>>
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345

# node resolv.conf
nameserver 10.0.2.2
search acme.internal svc.cluster.local
```

jessica-eng: NXDOMAIN from VPC resolver usually means either the private hosted zone isn't associated with the VPC, or there's a forwarding/resolver rule shadowing that suffix. Did the migration change account or VPC associations?

mark-dns: I checked Route53 for the zone name (`api.acme.internal` is under the private hosted zone `acme.internal`). Quick inventory: there are two hosted zones with that zone name across accounts: one private in the new account (ID ZP-NEW, associated to no VPCs), and one private in the old account (ID ZP-OLD, associated to the staging VPC only). Looks like during migration we created a hosted zone but never associated it to the prod VPC.

dmitri-netops: ah — that would explain NXDOMAIN. If the resolver doesn't see a matching private zone associated to that VPC, it returns NXDOMAIN (unless a resolver rule forwards it elsewhere). Any resolver rules pointing `acme.internal` to an on-prem forwarder?

mark-dns: ran `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=DomainName,Values=acme.internal` — there's a cross-account rule pointing to on-prem for `corp.acme.internal` but NOT for `acme.internal`. No forwarding in place for the exact suffix.

jessica-eng: repro steps we used: from a test pod in the affected VPC: `dig @<vpc-dns> api.acme.internal +trace` -> shows attempts then NXDOMAIN. Then on an EC2 in the prod VPC `nslookup api.acme.internal 10.0.2.2` -> NXDOMAIN.

infra-bot: deploy-note: migration runbook step 'associate-private-hosted-zone' was flagged as skipped for ACME (runbook: migrations/associate-hostedzone.md) :warning:

sam-support: Can we try associating ZP-NEW with the prod VPC (cross-account association requires owner id), or remove the stale ZP-OLD if it's the wrong one? Which is safer?

mark-dns: safest is to associate ZP-NEW to the prod VPC (explicitly via `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` with --vpc VPCRegion & --vpc VPCId and the zone owner account). But ZP-NEW is in the new account — we need account-owner consent for cross-account association. I requested a cross-account VPC association from ACME's infra team (they approved).

aws-support: FYI, cross-account association steps: call `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` from the zone owner account, or use the `AssociateVPCWithHostedZone` API with the owner credentials and include the target VPC info. Also verify that you don't have overlapping public hosted zones with the same name; Route53 resolves private zones before public ones for associated VPCs.

acme-customer: we gave permission for the association. Please proceed.

mark-dns: did the association. After association I cleared node-local-dns cache and restarted a pod to force new resolution. Commands I ran (owner account):
```bash
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZP-NEW --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0abc1234
# then on node
sudo systemctl restart node-local-dns || kubectl delete pod -n kube-system node-local-dns-xxxxx
kubectl rollout restart deployment/my-service
```

dmitri-netops: retested: `dig @10.0.2.2 api.acme.internal +short` -> `10.12.8.23` now resolves. TLS handshake fixed because cert SAN matched `api.acme.internal` on LB. :tada:

acme-customer: confirmed production traffic healthy, no more NXDOMAINs, thank you.

jessica-eng: Root cause summary for postmortem: hosted zone for `acme.internal` in new account created during migration but not associated to prod VPC. Result: VPC resolver had no record of private zone so returned NXDOMAIN. Remediation: associate zone to VPC, clear local caches, restart pods. Action items: add an automated runbook check that verifies post-migration associations for private hosted zones, and add a migration gating checklist item so 'associate-private-hosted-zone' can't be skipped.

sam-support: Filing follow-up ticket to add the runbook check + update migration playbook. Closing this thread once ops ticket is created. :white_check_mark:
